question:
(i) Explain how the electrostatic force between two point charges depends on the distance between them.
(ii) Two charges exert a force $F$ on each other when separated by distance $r$. Find the new force when the distance is made $2r$ and then $\frac{r}{2}$, keeping the charges unchanged.

options.A:
(i) For fixed charges, $F\propto\frac{1}{r^2}$
(ii) At $2r$, force is $\frac{F}{4}$; at $\frac{r}{2}$, force is $4F$
options.B:
(i) For fixed charges, $F\propto\frac{1}{r}$
(ii) At $2r$, force is $\frac{F}{2}$; at $\frac{r}{2}$, force is $2F$
options.C:
(i) For fixed charges, $F\propto r^2$
(ii) At $2r$, force is $4F$; at $\frac{r}{2}$, force is $\frac{F}{4}$
options.D:
(i) Force is independent of distance
(ii) Force remains $F$ in both cases
